newsitem.title: ITALY: Parmalat white knight bid for Canada's Ault Foods.
newsitem.headline: Parmalat white knight bid for Canada's Ault Foods.

text.p: Italy's largest publicly traded food company, Parmalat, appeared Monday as the white knight to ride to the rescue of Canada's Ault Foods in an agreed bid which topped a rival hostile bid from Canada's Saputo Group.

In its second acquisition in Canada in four months, Parmalat and its U.S. partner, Citicorp, have agreed to pay C$34 ($47) for each Ault share, above Saputo's C$28 bid ($39), making Parmalat's total bid worth C$415 million ($577 million).

Parmalat said it and Citicorp would raise C$150 million ($209 million) by a capital increase at its jointly owned holding Parmalat Canada Inc., with the rest of the C$415 million coming from a banking operation financed and underwritten by a group of banks including Citibank Canada, Bank of Nova Scotia and Bank of Montreal.
Parmalat stock on the Milan market were temporarily suspended ahead of the announcement, and when they reopened fell sharply to close down 5.98 percent at 2,311 lire ($1.37).

Analysts said the stock price was weakened with Parmalat making its second major acquisition in four months pushing up company debt, but in the long term this gave Parmalat a strong foothold in North America and expanded its global coverage.

In March, Parmalat purchased a majority stake in Canada's Beatrice Foods in a deal worth C$290 million ($403 million). In that deal, Parmalat allied itself with Citicorp, with Parmalat buying 75.1 percent of Beatrice and Citicorp 24.9 percent.

Parmalat said the Ault acquisition would be effected through a new company, Parmalat Foods Inc., 100 percent owned by Parmalat Canada Inc., which in turn is 75.1 percent owned by Parmalat and 24.9 percent by Citicorp after the Beatrice deal.
Ault Foods is a leading dairy company in Canada in the production and distribution of products such as cheese and butter. It has 10 production plants and 1,994 employees.

Parmalat added that Ault Foods has a 14 percent share of the Canadian national market in cheese and margarine, 36 percent in butter and some 26 percent of the liquid milk market in the province of Quebec.

The Italian company said a combined Beatrice and Ault would create a company with annual sales of almost C$2 billion ($2.78 billion) and operating profits of more than C$110 million ($153 million) -- and this would probably increase.
